newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss franc touches 11-month high versus mark.
newsitem.headline: Swiss franc touches 11-month high versus mark.

text.p: 1450 GMT - The Swiss franc ended firmer against the mark after it hit its highest level in roughly 11 months against the German currency in intraday trade on Wednesday.
The mark fell to as low as 81.08 Swiss centimes during the European session, the Swiss currency's highest level against the mark since it hit 80.82 centimes on August 30, 1996.
Traders said the franc had room for further gains against the mark, based on current fundamentals including uncertainty over the planned start of the European single currency.

The Swiss economy is showing signs of picking up, while the mark lost ground due to "a clear crisis" in the European Economic and Monetary Union, said Adam Beaudin, currency strategist at CSFB. The Swiss National Bank (SNB) also appeared to be less focused on the mark, after a long period in which it had tried to keep the franc from appreciating, he said.
* The dollar ended higher at 1.4860/4870 Swiss francs versus 1.4815/4825 at the close on Tuesday.
* The mark ended at 81.24/26 Swiss centimes versus 81.78/79 at Tuesday's close. -- Zurich Editorial, +41 1 631 7340
